solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Ingredient of fine Guinness, perhaps (6)

blocks.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
Sir Alec Guinness was a film star; 'perhaps' flags him as one example of his profession

annotation.surface: A drinker wonders what goes into a good pint of Guinness stout.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface wants Guinness the stout; it is Alec Guinness, the film actor of Star Wars and The Bridge on the River Kwai.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: one element that goes into a result is a contributing component of it.

entries.clue: Startle with a large member (5)

blocks.note: kept as written
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
a limb is a member of the body

annotation.surface: Someone is shocked by the sight of a very big limb, or a very big club member.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Member' is old-fashioned for a limb, which is why it gives ARM rather than a club member.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean to give someone a sudden fright.

entries.clue: Rich people fell into order before song and dance (3,4-2-2)

indicatorNotes.into: 'into' means going inside something, so HEW is put inside TELL
indicatorNotes.before: 'before' means ahead of, so the TELL group is written ahead of TO-DO

blocks.note: to tell someone to do something is to order them
to fell a tree is to hew it down
a song and dance is a fuss, a to-do

annotation.surface: Wealthy people have fallen into line ahead of a musical number.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fell' reads as the past tense of fall; it is the verb for cutting down a tree. 'Song and dance' is not a performance here but a fuss.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to be well-to-do is to be comfortably off, and the phrase with 'the' names such people as a class.

entries.clue: Bones for stays (7)

blocks.note: a noun: what is left of a body after death
a verb: is left behind, does not go

annotation.surface: Bones used as stays, like the whalebone stiffeners in a corset.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stays' suggests corset stays, whose whalebone ties in with 'bones'; it is the verb, as in 'he stays put'.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses of one word: as a noun it names a corpse or skeleton, and as a verb it means continues to be there.

entries.clue: Pieces match, but not on paper (8)

blocks.note: chess or draughts pieces are men
two accounts that tally match

annotation.surface: The jigsaw pieces fit together, yet nothing has been written down.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pieces' suggests jigsaw bits; board-game pieces are MEN.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by contrast: working in your head is the opposite of writing it down.

entries.clue: Ordinary wordplay for 9 Across? (6-2-3-4)

blocks.note: the straight definition: moderate, unremarkable
the answer, read as instructions, builds 9 Across: the central letter of 'the', then a road abbreviated

annotation.surface: A puzzle-maker asks what plain, everyday clue would lead to 9 Across.
annotation.walkthrough: Read the answer as instructions: the middle of THE is H, and a road is AVE, short for avenue. H + AVE is HAVE, 9 Across.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: a middle-of-the-road taste or opinion is unadventurous and mainstream.

entries.clue: Bat welcome to devour rubbish (7)

indicatorNotes.to devour: what you devour ends up inside you, so NICE takes TAT inside itself

blocks.note: welcome news is nice news
tat is cheap junk

annotation.surface: A bat, glad to be fed, tucks into refuse.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bat' wants to be the animal; it is the verb, as in 'not bat an eyelid'.
annotation.definitionFit: A rare word: to wink or blink, the sense of bat in 'she didn't bat an eye'.

entries.clue: Fitting a soft type of shirt (3)

blocks.note: kept as written
p (piano) is the musical instruction for soft
a T-shirt

annotation.surface: A tailor is fitting someone for a soft shirt.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fitting' looks like a tailor's fitting; it is the adjective meaning suitable.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both adjectives mean suitable for the occasion.

entries.clue: Insanely difficult to eat duck cooked with onions (9)

indicatorNotes.difficult: something difficult is awkward and unmanageable, so the letters are put out of order
indicatorNotes.to eat: what is eaten ends up inside, so the rearranged letters take O in

blocks.note: anagram fodder
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, O

annotation.surface: Someone finds a duck with onions absurdly hard to eat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Duck' sits right beside 'cooked', but it is the cricket score of zero, O.
annotation.definitionFit: A cookery term: dishes named after Lyon are prepared with sliced onions.

entries.clue: Feel divide, left out (4)

indicatorNotes.out: something that is out is no longer present, so L is dropped from the word

blocks.note: to halve is to divide in two
the standard abbreviation, removed

annotation.surface: A divided nation senses that the political left has been shut out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Feel' looks odd here; Collins gives the answer the sense 'to experience or undergo'.
annotation.definitionFit: A dictionary sense: to experience a pain or a feeling, as in 'I have a headache'.

entries.clue: Good offices will stock cold remedy (10)

indicatorNotes.will stock: a shop that stocks an item holds it inside, so MEDIATION holds C

blocks.note: good offices is the diplomatic term for help in settling a dispute
C for cold, as on a tap

annotation.surface: A decent office will keep something for colds in its first-aid cabinet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Good offices' is the diplomatic phrase for a go-between's help, not a nice workplace.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a drug given to cure or relieve an illness.

entries.clue: Four quarts of fluid in large oil lamp (8,6)

indicatorNotes.fluid: something fluid has no fixed shape, so the letters can flow into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 14 letters

annotation.surface: A big oil lamp holds four quarts of fuel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fluid' reads as the lamp oil; it is the signal to rearrange. The British measure is bigger than the US one.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by measure: the British unit of liquid volume is made up of four quarts, about 4.5 litres.

entries.clue: See dame boarding sub last (2,3,6)

indicatorNotes.boarding: a boarding passenger goes inside the vehicle, so DBE goes inside between LOAN and HOLD

blocks.note: to sub someone is to lend them money; a sub is an advance
a dame holds the DBE, Dame Commander of the British Empire
the weather will hold = it will last

annotation.surface: A woman climbs aboard a submarine at the last moment.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sub' suggests a submarine and 'boarding' climbing aboard; a sub is an advance on wages.
annotation.definitionFit: An exclamation: both call attention to something surprising, like 'Look!'.

entries.clue: Name is given to Greek nymph (8)

blocks.note: to name someone is to call them
kept as written
only 'to' is kept

annotation.surface: A Greek nymph is being given a name.
annotation.walkthrough: The nymph was a follower of Artemis whom Zeus turned into a bear; her name is also a moon of Jupiter.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a named nymph of Greek myth, later set among the stars as the Great Bear.

entries.clue: Lorry that man used to carry fine plant (9)

indicatorNotes.used to carry: a thing that carries a load holds it, so HE holds OK inside

blocks.note: an artic is British slang for an articulated lorry, a tractor-trailer
he = that man
fine = OK

annotation.surface: A truck driver uses his lorry to haul a good plant.
annotation.walkthrough: A lorry is the British word for a truck, and an articulated one is called an artic.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a thistle-like vegetable grown for its edible flower heads.

entries.clue: Some retaliate as well as others (2,4)

indicatorNotes.Some: 'some' means a part and not the whole, so only part of the next word is used

blocks.note: the six letters after the R, stopping before the final TE

annotation.surface: Some people hit back, and so do others.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer is Latin for 'and others', the full form of et al. in lists of authors.
annotation.definitionFit: A Latin phrase: literally 'and other things', used to mean 'and the rest as well'.

entries.clue: Biological material sent out to Mars (6)

indicatorNotes.sent out: letters sent out are scattered, so they come back in a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder

annotation.surface: Samples of living matter are dispatched to the red planet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sent out to Mars' sounds like a space mission, with the sample as its payload.
annotation.definitionFit: A technical term: the supporting tissue of an organ, or the matrix inside a chloroplast.

entries.clue: Soccer club stadium incorporates small lake (7)

indicatorNotes.incorporates: to incorporate is to take into the body, so ARENA takes S inside

blocks.note: an arena is a stadium
S for small, as in clothing sizes
L for lake, as on maps

annotation.surface: A football club's ground has a little pond built into it.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one sentence about a club's ground, which hides that 'stadium' is only a piece of wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the north London football club.

entries.clue: Old model stuck, cut by old kind of sword (3-5)

indicatorNotes.cut by: a word cut by a letter is split open by it, so O goes into WEDGED

blocks.note: the Model T was Ford's old car
stuck fast = wedged
O for old

annotation.surface: An old statue is jammed in place and slashed by an antique sword.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Old model' wants to be an elderly fashion model; it is the Model T Ford, so just T.
annotation.definitionFit: A description as definition: a blade sharpened on both sides, the sword in the idiom for a mixed blessing.

entries.clue: Loose coat used for sweeping (7)

blocks.note: a protective garment worn over clothes for dirty work
an adjective here: broad, taking everything in

annotation.surface: A cleaner wears a loose coat while doing the sweeping.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sweeping' looks like work with a broom; it is the adjective meaning broad, general.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses of one word: a British work coat, and an adjective meaning comprehensive.

entries.clue: Look here, it says “X marks the spot” (5-9)

annotation.definition: Look here, it says “X marks the spot”

blocks.note: the setter's reading: a note in a text telling the reader where else to look
the surface pushes a treasure map, but read literally an X is a cross, and marking a spot with it refers you there

annotation.surface: A treasure map's instruction: look here, where X marks the spot.
annotation.walkthrough: The pirate map is the decoy. A cross marking a spot is literally a reference made by a cross.
annotation.definitionFit: A publishing term: a note directing the reader to another place in the same text.

entries.clue: “X” — author on strike (5)

blocks.note: X is the Greek letter chi
the author of a clue speaks of himself as ME

annotation.surface: A writer known only as X has walked out on strike.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On strike' paints a picket line; the definition is the strike of a clock.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for a clock or bell sounding the hour.

entries.clue: Terrible female novelist in Italian town (10)

blocks.note: the Gorgons were monstrous women of Greek myth, like Medusa
Émile Zola, the French novelist

annotation.surface: A dreadful woman writer is living in a small Italian town.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer suggests the blue cheese, which is named after this town near Milan.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a town in Lombardy that gave its name to a cheese.

entries.clue: State proposal that’s realistic when delivered (3)

indicatorNotes.when delivered: a speech is delivered by being spoken, so the word is said out loud

blocks.note: British informal for a plan that will work; in a non-rhotic accent the final R is not pronounced

annotation.surface: A government proposal only looks realistic once it is presented.
annotation.walkthrough: A goer is British informal for a workable idea. 'State' looks like a verb; it is a region of India.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: one of India's states, on the west coast.

entries.clue: Sick? Not very, miss (4)

indicatorNotes.Not: 'not' excludes what follows, so V is taken out

blocks.note: to be sick is to vomit
V for very, removed

annotation.surface: Someone asks a young woman whether she is ill, and is told only slightly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Miss' looks like a form of address; it is the verb, to leave out.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean to leave something out.

entries.clue: Elaborate action parts for chase (8)

indicatorNotes.parts for: to part is to separate, as a crowd parts for someone, so DEED opens to let TAIL in

blocks.note: a deed is an action
to tail someone is to follow or chase them

annotation.surface: An action film's intricate scenes set up a car chase.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Action parts' sounds like roles in an action film; 'parts' is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the adjective means intricate, full of particulars.

entries.clue: Female can notice inside information that’s false (6)

indicatorNotes.inside: 'inside' means within, so AD is placed within LIES

blocks.note: false information is lies
an ad, an advertisement, is a public notice

annotation.surface: A woman may spot the falsehood buried within a report.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Female can' reads as a capable woman; can is US slang for a toilet.
annotation.definitionFit: A British usage: the women's toilet, with can as slang for toilet.
